business_logic: '- Build department_posting_base from postings: - Dimensions defaulted via COALESCE: department=''Unknown Department'', team=''Unknown Team'', location=''Unknown Location'', level=''Unknown Level'', commitment_type=''Unknown Commitment''.
- avg_applications_per_posting = total applications / active postings, rounded to 1 decimal; NULL when active postings=0 (later COALESCE to 0).
- interview_hours_per_hire = total_interview_hours / total hires, rounded to 1 decimal; NULL when no hires (later COALESCE to 0).
- applications_per_hire = sum(total_applications) / total hires, rounded to 1 decimal; NULL when no hires (later COALESCE to 0).

- business_logic_score: compute 1 minus the ratio of total business logic violations to the overall total records, then multiply by 100; return NULL if the denominator is zero.

Implementation includes raw-field mapping and timestamp parsing in staging, event-key generation, invalid-row filtering/nullification, latest-record models, daily aggregates and calendar spines, and mart entities.
Invalid primary/event identifiers are filtered where the contract directs deletion; malformed optional fields are nullified where specified.
Residual impact: discarded invalid rows are not available to downstream analytics, and nullified optional values reduce the detail available for analysis.
A number of advanced/complex model outputs remain simplified relative to the contract.

In particular, product-health and conversion-funnel outputs omit some of their prescribed breakdowns and full calculations; the DQ report is currently a summary-only row; RFM account-level metrics are NULL placeholders; and several advanced marts (including lifecycle insights and executive dashboard) use abbreviated/defaulted derivations.

business_logic: 'Build per-customer behavior and segmentation by: - Source inputs: - Marketo (intermediate.int_customer360__marketo) per lead_id - Stripe (intermediate.int_customer360__stripe) per customer_id - Zendesk (intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk) per user_id - Identity map (intermediate.int_customer360__source_matches) providing the cross-platform ID linkage - Per-platform metrics: - Marketo: - marketo_first_touch = created_at; marketo_last_activity = updated_at - marketo_engagement_score: - 0 if is_unsubscribed = true or is_email_invalid = true - else 3 if days between created_at and updated_at < 30 - else 2 if < 90 - else 1 - has_organization_data = 1 if organization_name_no_suffix not null and length > 3 else 0 - has_phone_contact = 1 if phone or mobile_phone present else 0 - address_completeness_score: - 3 if country_code, state_code, and city all present - 2 if country_code present and at least one of state_code or city present - 1 if only country_code present - 0 otherwise - Stripe: - stripe_first_transaction = created_at; stripe_last_activity = updated_at - stripe_engagement_score: - 0 if is_deleted = true - 1 if is_delinquent = true (and not deleted) - else 4 if days between created_at and updated_at < 30 - else 3 if < 90 - else 2 - payment_reliability_score: - 3 if is_delinquent = false and is_deleted = false - 1 if is_delinquent = true and is_deleted = false - 0 otherwise - billing_completeness_score: - 2 if customer_address_line_1 and customer_country_code present - 1 if only customer_country_code present - 0 otherwise - Zendesk: - zendesk_first_contact = created_at; zendesk_last_activity = updated_at - zendesk_engagement_score: - 0 if is_suspended = true or is_deleted = true - 1 if is_active = false - else 4 if days between created_at and updated_at < 30 - else 3 if < 90 - else 2 - org_relationship_strength: - 2 if organization_id and organization_name_no_suffix present - 1 if only organization_id present - 0 otherwise - Join and aggregate: - Left join per-platform metrics to source_matches on respective IDs - primary_email = coalesce(Marketo.email, Stripe.email, Zendesk.email); rows with NULL primary_email are excluded - email_domain and primary_organization use the same COALESCE order (Marketo, then Stripe, then Zendesk) - customer_first_touchpoint = the earliest of the three per-platform first-touch timestamps - customer_last_activity = the latest of the three per-platform last-activity timestamps - If any of the three timestamps is NULL, the earliest/latest result is NULL - marketo_engagement/stripe_engagement/zendesk_engagement = respective per-platform scores with NULL → 0 - composite_engagement_score = weighted average (weights: Marketo 0.3, Stripe 0.5, Zendesk 0.2), rounded to two decimals and stored with one decimal precision - in_marketo/in_stripe/in_zendesk = 1 if respective joined record exists, else 0 - organization_data_quality = coalesce(has_organization_data,0) + coalesce(billing_completeness_score,0) + coalesce(org_relationship_strength,0) - has_contact_phone = coalesce(has_phone_contact, 0) - address_data_quality = coalesce(address_completeness_score,0) + coalesce(billing_completeness_score,0) - marketing_to_sales_days = days between Marketo first touch and Stripe first transaction only if both present; else NULL - sales_to_support_days = days between Stripe first transaction and Zendesk first contact only if both present; else NULL - account_age_days = days between the earliest available first-touch and current_date; NULL if the earliest is NULL - customer_maturity (derived from the same earliest timestamp vs current_date): - ''New Customer'' if < 90 days - ''Growing Relationship'' if < 365 days - ''Established Customer'' if < 1095 days - ''Long-term Customer'' otherwise (including when the start date is NULL) - customer_journey_pattern based on platform presence, evaluated in this order: - ''Full Journey'' if all three present - ''Marketing to Sales'' if Marketo and Stripe - ''Sales to Support'' if Stripe and Zendesk - ''Marketing to Support'' if Marketo and Zendesk - ''Marketing Only'' if only Marketo - ''Sales Only'' if only Stripe - ''Support Only'' if only Zendesk - ''Unknown'' otherwise - payment_reliability = coalesce(Stripe.payment_reliability_score, 0) - Classification: - customer_segment (first match wins): - ''Champion'' if composite_engagement_score >= 3.5 and payment_reliability >= 2 - ''Loyal Customer'' if composite_engagement_score >= 3.0 and customer_journey_pattern = ''Full Journey'' - ''Potential Loyalist'' if composite_engagement_score >= 2.5 and payment_reliability >= 2 - ''New Customer'' if composite_engagement_score >= 2.0 and account_age_days < 90 - ''At Risk'' if composite_engagement_score >= 1.5 - ''Hibernating'' if composite_engagement_score > 0 - ''Lost'' otherwise - churn_risk_level: - ''High Risk'' if payment_reliability = 0 or composite_engagement_score < 1 - ''Medium Risk'' if composite_engagement_score < 2 and account_age_days > 365 - ''Medium Risk'' if customer_last_activity is more than 90 days ago - ''Low Risk'' otherwise (including when comparisons evaluate to NULL) - recommended_action based on customer_segment: - ''Upsell/Cross-sell'' for ''Champion'' or ''Loyal Customer'' - ''Engagement Campaign'' for ''Potential Loyalist'' - ''Onboarding Focus'' for ''New Customer'' - ''Win-back Campaign'' for ''At Risk'' - ''Reactivation Campaign'' for ''Hibernating'' - ''Recovery Campaign'' otherwise - Output filter and ordering: - Keep only rows where primary_email is not NULL - Order rows by composite_engagement_score descending, then account_age_days descending'

business_logic: 'Starting from intermediate.int_customer360__customer_behavior_analysis (one row per resolved customer), compute lifecycle metrics and enrichments: - Activity windows and recency: - days_since_last_activity = number of days between customer_last_activity and today; NULL if customer_last_activity is missing.

- Lifecycle stage (first match wins): - ''Acquisition'' if account_age_days ≤ 30 - ''Activation'' if account_age_days ≤ 90 and last_activity within 30 days - ''Growth'' if account_age_days ≤ 365 and last_activity within 60 days - ''Maturity'' if account_age_days > 365 and last_activity within 90 days - ''Dormant'' if last_activity older than 180 days - Else ''Retention'' - Note: NULL account_age_days or last_activity causes earlier conditions to fail and typically falls through to ''Retention''.
- Cohort and platform consistency: - acquisition_cohort_month = month of the first touchpoint (truncated to month); NULL if first_touchpoint is missing.
NULL in any flag leads to the else path → 1.
- recency_score (1–5) by days_since_last_activity: 5 (≤7), 4 (≤30), 3 (≤60), 2 (≤180), else 1; NULL days_since_last_activity maps to 1.

- growth_potential (first match wins): - ''High Growth Potential'' if lifecycle_stage in (''Acquisition'',''Activation'') and customer_health_score ≥ 3.5 - ''Expansion Ready'' if lifecycle_stage = ''Growth'' and platform_consistency_score ≥ 2 - ''Upsell Candidate'' if lifecycle_stage = ''Maturity'' and customer_health_score ≥ 4.0 - ''Stable Account'' if lifecycle_stage = ''Retention'' and customer_health_score ≥ 3.0 - ''Reactivation Needed'' if lifecycle_stage = ''Dormant'' - Else ''Monitor'' - action_priority (INT, first match wins): - 5 if churn-probability mapping ≥ 0.65 - 4 if lifecycle_stage = ''Acquisition'' and customer_health_score ≥ 3.5 - 4 if lifecycle_stage = ''Growth'' and platform_consistency_score ≥ 2 - 3 if customer_health_score ≥ 4.0 and estimated_customer_value ≥ 3000 - 3 if churn-probability mapping ≥ 0.35 - Else 2 - acquisition_year = year of acquisition_cohort_month; acquisition_month = month number; months_since_acquisition = whole months between acquisition_cohort_month and today; NULL if acquisition_cohort_month is NULL.
- acquisition_season: ''Holiday Season'' if month in (11,12,1); ''Summer Season'' if in (6,7,8); ''Spring Season'' if in (3,4,5); else ''Fall Season'' (default for NULL or not matched).

business_logic: '- Read pass-through datasets: - marts.customer360__mapping as mapping (provides marketo_lead_id and stripe_customer_id per customer360_id) - staging.stg_customer360__country_codes as country_codes - staging.stg_customer360__state_territory_codes as state_codes - Build Marketo addresses (inner join mapping.marketo_lead_id = int_customer360__marketo.lead_id): - Primary address: include rows where address_line_1 is not NULL; set source_system = "marketo", address_type = "primary", priority = 1; select address_line_1, address_line_2, city, state_code, country_code, postal_code - Billing address: include rows where billing_address_line_1 is not NULL; set source_system = "marketo", address_type = "billing", priority = 2; map billing_* fields to output columns - Build Stripe addresses (inner join mapping.stripe_customer_id = int_customer360__stripe.customer_id): - Customer address: include rows where customer_address_line_1 is not NULL; set source_system = "stripe", address_type = "customer", priority = 1; map customer_* fields - Shipping address: include rows where shipping_address_line_1 is not NULL; set source_system = "stripe", address_type = "shipping", priority = 2; map shipping_* fields - Union all Marketo and Stripe address rows; no de-duplication; only addresses with non-NULL address_line_1 are included.

- Enrich with geographic names via left joins: - state: join state_codes on (state_code AND country_code) to derive state_territory; unmatched → NULL - country and country_alt_name: join country_codes on alpha-2 country code; unmatched → NULL - Compute rank: per customer360_id, assign row numbers ordered by priority ascending; within the same priority, order is unspecified and non-deterministic.

- Enrich with platform data via left joins on platform IDs: - Marketo: intermediate.int_customer360__marketo on lead_id - Stripe: intermediate.int_customer360__stripe on customer_id - Zendesk: intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk on user_id - Filter: exclude rows where primary_email is NULL; no de-duplication beyond joins.
Activity recency and counts - days/weeks/months_since_last_activity: difference between customer_last_activity and current_date by unit; returns NULL if customer_last_activity is NULL.
- active_channel_count: integer sum (in_marketo + in_stripe + in_zendesk); if any flag is NULL the sum becomes NULL; expected domain is 0–3 from 0/1 flags.

Engagement velocity, momentum, maturity (rule-based categories) - engagement_velocity (uses activity recency and composite_engagement_score): - <=7 days and score>=3.0 → Accelerating - <=14 days and score>=2.5 → Steady High - <=30 days and score>=2.0 → Steady Medium - <=60 days → Declining - <=90 days → Slow - else → Stagnant - activity_momentum (uses days_since_last_activity and composite_engagement_score): - <=7 days and score>=3.5 → High Momentum - <=14 days and score>=3.0 → Medium Momentum - <=30 days and score>=2.0 → Low Momentum - <=60 days → Losing Momentum - else → No Momentum - engagement_maturity (uses account_age_days and active_channel_count): - age>=365 and channels>=3 → Mature Multi-channel - age>=180 and channels>=2 → Developing Multi-channel - age>=90 and channels>=1 → Single Channel Engaged - age<90 → Early Stage - else → Minimal Engagement Channel scores and depths - marketing_engagement_score: if in_marketo=1 and is_unsubscribed=false and is_email_invalid=false then round(marketo_engagement × (1 − days since last Marketo update / 90), 2); else 0; may be negative; if the last update timestamp is NULL the result is NULL in the true branch.

- sales_engagement_score: if in_stripe=1 and is_deleted=false and is_delinquent=false then round(stripe_engagement × (1 − days since last Stripe update / 60), 2); else 0; may be negative; NULL if the last update timestamp is NULL in the true branch.

- support_engagement_score: if in_zendesk=1 and is_active=true and is_suspended=false and is_deleted=false then round(zendesk_engagement × (1 − days since last Zendesk update / 120), 2); else 0; may be negative; NULL if the last update timestamp is NULL in the true branch.

- primary_engagement_channel: choose the channel with the highest raw engagement; ties break in order Marketing Driven > Sales Driven > Support Driven; if comparisons do not resolve (e.g., NULL inputs) fallback is Balanced.

Cross-platform and composite scores - cross_platform_consistency: round( average of raw engagement across platforms where in_*=1, 2 decimals ); returns NULL if no active platforms or if any included operand (flags or raw engagements) is NULL.
- activity_efficiency: round(composite_engagement_score divided by active_channel_count, 2); NULL if active_channel_count is 0 or NULL.
- weighted_engagement_score: round(0.3×marketing_engagement_score (NULL→0) + 0.5×sales_engagement_score (NULL→0) + 0.2×support_engagement_score (NULL→0), 2); can be negative.

business_logic: 'Starting from intermediate.int_customer360__customer_lifecycle_metrics (aliased lm), compute RFM metrics and value segments, then portfolio and recommendation metrics; finally filter to rows where primary_email is not NULL and sort for presentation (sorting does not affect metric values).
- RFM score string: concatenate recency_score, frequency_score, and monetary_score with no delimiter in R-F-M order; if any component is NULL the result is NULL.
- RFM average: average of recency_score, frequency_score, and monetary_score, rounded to 2 decimals; NULL if any component is NULL.

- Expected annual revenue: compute adjusted_ltv × (1 − churn_probability) divided by the age denominator (account_age_days/365.0 when account_age_days≥365, otherwise 1); round to 2 decimals; returns NULL if adjusted_ltv or churn_probability is NULL.

- Portfolio contribution pct: adjusted_ltv divided by the total adjusted_ltv across all customers in the portfolio (computed before the final email filter), multiplied by 100 and rounded to 4 decimals; NULL when the portfolio total is 0 or NULL.
- Revenue risk percentage: churn_probability expressed as a percentage rounded to 2 decimals; NULL if adjusted_ltv is NULL or zero.
- Final filter and ordering: keep only rows with primary_email IS NOT NULL; order by investment_priority_score desc, adjusted_ltv desc, customer_health_score desc.'

- Derive account_size_segment from annual_revenue: - >= 10,000,000 → "Enterprise" - >= 1,000,000 and < 10,000,000 → "Mid-Market" - >= 100,000 and < 1,000,000 → "SMB" - > 0 and < 100,000 → "Small" - Else (NULL or <= 0) → "Unknown" - Derive geographic_region using case-insensitive billing_country matching: - North America if in {US, USA, UNITED STATES, CANADA, CA} - Europe if in {UK, UNITED KINGDOM, FRANCE, GERMANY, SPAIN, ITALY, NETHERLANDS, BELGIUM, SWEDEN, NORWAY, DENMARK, FINLAND, IRELAND, PORTUGAL, AUSTRIA, SWITZERLAND} - Asia-Pacific if in {CHINA, JAPAN, INDIA, AUSTRALIA, SINGAPORE, SOUTH KOREA, THAILAND, MALAYSIA, INDONESIA, PHILIPPINES, VIETNAM, NEW ZEALAND} - Latin America if in {BRAZIL, MEXICO, ARGENTINA, CHILE, COLOMBIA, PERU, VENEZUELA, ECUADOR, BOLIVIA, URUGUAY, PARAGUAY} - Else (including NULL or blanks) → "Other" - Set account_age_days to NULL and account_maturity_stage to constant "Unknown" (placeholders).
- industry_normalized: remove leading/trailing spaces when industry is present; else NULL; original casing and internal spacing preserved.

- data_completeness_score: sum four 25-point checks, then round to two decimals (scores remain whole numbers 0/25/50/75/100): - +25 if website is present and non-blank after trimming - +25 if industry is present and non-blank after trimming - +25 if annual_revenue is present and > 0 - +25 if number_of_employees is present and > 0 - is_high_value_account: true if annual_revenue >= 5,000,000, or if account_type equals "Customer" and annual_revenue >= 1,000,000; otherwise false; NULL revenue never meets thresholds.'

- Pass through source attributes and derive: - lead_name: If both first_name and last_name are present, set to "first_name last_name"; if only last_name is present, set to last_name; otherwise null.
If a required date is missing, the result is null.
- conversion_time_days: For converted leads only, the number of days between the date parts of created_date and converted_date; null otherwise or when dates are missing.
Null lead_source is treated as Other.

- lead_quality_score: Integer score (0–100) computed as the sum of points: +20 for an email containing "@" and a later ".", +15 if phone or mobile_phone is present, +10 if industry is non-empty after trimming, +15 if annual_revenue is greater than 0, +10 if number_of_employees is greater than 0, +20 if lead_source equals referral, website, or partner referral (case-insensitive), and +10 if company is non-empty after trimming and does not contain test/example/demo (case-insensitive).

- conversion_speed_category: For converted leads with a non-null conversion_time_days, assign Fast Track for <=7 days, Standard for <=30 days, Slow for <=90 days, and Extended for >90 days; otherwise null.

- Compute rolling_metrics per (account_id, source_relation), ordered by date_day: - 7-day rolling averages: for each day, average spend, clicks, and impressions across the current day and up to six prior days; averages ignore NULLs and use smaller windows at the start.
- Cost per conversion: spend per conversion; NULL when conversions <= 0.

- performance_score: clamp to 0–100 for the sum of: CTR*10; ROAS*10 capped at 50; +20 if cost_per_conversion < 50; and either +10 if clicks_7d_avg > 100 else + (clicks_7d_avg / 10); may be NULL if clicks_7d_avg is NULL.
- spend_mom_change_pct: percent change vs the 30-day lag of spend when the lag > 0; rounded to 2 decimals; else NULL.
- conversions_mom_change_pct: percent change vs the 30-day lag of conversions when the lag > 0; rounded to 2 decimals; else NULL.
- Final select joins account_scoring to account_info on (account_id, source_relation) with a left join; account_name, currency_code, and time_zone may be NULL if no match.
- Apply final filters: keep rows where spend >= 0, clicks >= 0, impressions >= 0, conversions >= 0, date_day IS NOT NULL, and account_id IS NOT NULL.

If cost_per_conversion is missing, the score is NULL.

- Acquisition cohort: for each account_id, find the earliest date_day with conversions > 0 and use the first day of that month; set to NULL if the account has no conversions.
- Days since first conversion: calendar days between the account’s first conversion date and the current date_day; NULL if no first conversion date.
- Channel and lifecycle: take advertising_channel_type, advertising_channel_subtype, and lifecycle_stage (as campaign_lifecycle_stage) from cc; these may be NULL.
- Daily portfolio counts per account_id and date_day (based on joined cc rows; NULLs ignored): - active_campaigns_count: distinct campaign_id count.
- Derived economics per row: - customer_acquisition_cost (CAC): cumulative_acquisition_cost divided by cumulative_conversions, rounded to 2 decimals when cumulative_conversions > 0; otherwise NULL.

- estimated_payback_days: cost_per_conversion divided by average conversion value on the row (conversions_value divided by conversions), scaled to 30 days and rounded to a whole number when cost_per_conversion > 0 and conversions_value > 0; otherwise NULL.
- customer_maturity_stage from days_since_first_conversion: Not Acquired (NULL), ≤30 New Customer, ≤90 Early Stage, ≤365 Developing Customer, ≤1095 Mature Customer, else Long-term Customer.
- cac_vs_cohort_pct: ((customer_acquisition_cost − cohort_avg_cac) / cohort_avg_cac) * 100 rounded to 2 decimals when cohort_avg_cac > 0; otherwise NULL.
- ltv_vs_cohort_pct: ((average_customer_ltv − cohort_avg_ltv) / cohort_avg_ltv) * 100 rounded to 2 decimals when cohort_avg_ltv > 0; otherwise NULL.
- Final filter: keep rows where cumulative_conversions > 0 or spend > 0, and date_day and account_id are not NULL; ordered by account_id ascending and date_day descending.'

business_logic: '- Group campaign-level rows by platform, account_id normalized by replacing NULL with ''0'' and casting to text, and date_day.
- Set segmentation fields not used at account level to NULL: ad_network_type, device, interaction_event_types.

- Aggregate totals across all campaigns in each group: - Sum impressions, clicks, interactions, cost, conversions, conversions_value, and view_through_conversions; missing values are ignored, and if all values are missing the result is NULL.

- Derived metrics (computed from the aggregated totals): - Click-through rate (percent) = total clicks / total impressions × 100, rounded to 4 decimals; returns 0 if total impressions is not greater than 0; returns NULL if total clicks is NULL while impressions are positive.
- Cost per click = total cost / total clicks, rounded to 2 decimals; returns 0 if total clicks is not greater than 0; returns NULL if total cost is NULL while clicks are positive.

- Cost per thousand impressions = total cost / total impressions × 1000, rounded to 2 decimals; returns 0 if total impressions is not greater than 0; returns NULL if total cost is NULL while impressions are positive.
- Cost per conversion = total cost / total conversions, rounded to 2 decimals; returns 0 if total conversions is not greater than 0; returns NULL if total cost is NULL while conversions are positive.
- _dbt_loaded_at is the latest timestamp across grouped rows (MAX); if all inputs are missing, the result is NULL.'

- rfm_segment (evaluated top-to-bottom; first match wins): - RECENT and total_conversions>=5 and total_revenue>=1000 → CHAMPIONS - (RECENT or MODERATE) and total_conversions>=3 and total_revenue>=500 → LOYAL_CUSTOMERS - RECENT and total_conversions<=2 and total_revenue>=100 → POTENTIAL_LOYALISTS - RECENT and total_conversions<=2 and total_revenue<=100 → NEW_CUSTOMERS - MODERATE and total_conversions>=3 and total_revenue<=200 → PROMISING - (DORMANT or INACTIVE) and total_conversions>=3 and total_revenue>=500 → CUSTOMERS_NEEDING_ATTENTION - (DORMANT or INACTIVE) and total_conversions<=2 and total_revenue>=200 → ABOUT_TO_SLEEP - (DORMANT or INACTIVE) and total_conversions>=3 and total_revenue<=200 → AT_RISK - INACTIVE and total_conversions<=2 and total_revenue<=100 → LOST - ELSE → OTHERS - customer_health_score (0–100 integer): sum four components, then bound the result to 0–100: - recency_status: RECENT→25; ELSE→0 - engagement_level: HIGHLY_ENGAGED→25; MODERATELY_ENGAGED→15; LIGHTLY_ENGAGED→5; ELSE→0 - conversion_behavior: FREQUENT_CONVERTER→25; REPEAT_CONVERTER→15; SINGLE_CONVERTER→5; ELSE→0 - customer_roas: >=3.0→25; >=2.0→15; >=1.0→10; >0→5; ELSE→0 - churn_risk_level (evaluated in listed order; first match wins): - recency_status=INACTIVE → HIGH_CHURN_RISK - recency_status=DORMANT and engagement_level=SINGLE_INTERACTION → MEDIUM_CHURN_RISK - customer_roas < 0.5 → UNPROFITABLE_RISK - ELSE → LOW_RISK - clv_potential (evaluated in listed order; first match wins): - total_revenue>=1000 and customer_roas>=2.0 → HIGH_POTENTIAL - total_revenue>=500 or customer_roas>=1.5 → MEDIUM_POTENTIAL - total_revenue>=100 → LOW_POTENTIAL - ELSE → MINIMAL_POTENTIAL - marketing_recommendation (evaluated in listed order; first match wins): - RECENT and total_conversions>=5 and total_revenue>=1000 → "VIP treatment, exclusive offers, loyalty program" - (RECENT or MODERATE) and total_conversions>=3 → "Retention campaigns, upsell opportunities" - RECENT and total_conversions<=2 and total_revenue>=100 → "Frequency building campaigns, personalized recommendations" - RECENT and total_conversions<=2 and total_revenue<=100 → "Onboarding campaigns, educational content" - (DORMANT or INACTIVE) and total_conversions>=3 → "Re-engagement campaigns, win-back offers" - INACTIVE → "Last-chance campaigns, deep discounts" - ELSE → "Standard marketing campaigns" - investment_priority (evaluated in listed order; first match wins; uses computed churn_risk_level with customer_value_tier and customer_health_score): - customer_value_tier=HIGH_VALUE and churn_risk_level=LOW_RISK → RETAIN_EXPAND - customer_value_tier in (MEDIUM_VALUE, LOW_VALUE) and customer_health_score>=60 → DEVELOP_NURTURE - churn_risk_level in (HIGH_CHURN_RISK, MEDIUM_CHURN_RISK) → URGENT_INTERVENTION - churn_risk_level=UNPROFITABLE_RISK → WIN_BACK_OR_IGNORE - ELSE → STANDARD_TREATMENT - Benchmarking percentiles (computed over the filtered dataset): - clv_percentile: percentile rank across all rows sorted by total_revenue ascending; NULLs sort after non-NULLs; ties share the same percentile; values range from 0 to 1.

Metrics null policy: - crash_count = coalesce(source crashes, 0).
- daily_average_rating and total_average_rating come from Google Play ratings; they are NULL when no rating row exists.

Rolling windows and lags (partitioned by app_name and platform; ordered by date_day; row-based using available records only): - 7-row averages: crash_rate_7d_avg = average of crash_rate_per_thousand over up to the last 7 records (including current); uninstall_rate_7d_avg = average of uninstall_rate_percentage over the same; rating_7d_avg = average of daily_average_rating over the same (NULL if all values in the window are NULL).
Trends (default to 0 when insufficient history or NULL inputs): - rating_trend_7d = daily_average_rating minus rating_7d_ago when both exist; else 0.
Output filter and timestamp: - Include only rows where date_day, app_name, and platform are not NULL.

business_logic: 'Build analytics in stages: - Filter projects to those with a non-null project_name.
- Derive schedule metrics: - planned_duration_days: whole days from start (created_at) to deadline if a deadline exists; otherwise null.
- remaining_days: whole days from today to deadline if a deadline exists; otherwise null.
- completion_rate_per_day: completion_percentage divided by elapsed_days, rounded to 4 decimals; null if elapsed_days is not positive.

- Resource/workload metrics: - avg_tasks_per_assignee: if total_tasks > 0, divide total_tasks by max(1, unique_assignees) and round to 2 decimals; if unique_assignees is null in this case, the result is null; otherwise 0.
- team_size_category by unique_assignees: 0 → no_team; 1 → solo_project; 2–3 → small_team; 4–7 → medium_team; 8–15 → large_team; else enterprise_team (null maps to enterprise_team).
- project_size_category by total_tasks: 0–5 → micro_project; 6–20 → small_project; 21–50 → medium_project; 51–100 → large_project; else enterprise_project (null maps to enterprise_project).

- estimated_days_to_completion: when completion_rate_per_day > 0 and completion_percentage < 100, (100 − completion_percentage) divided by completion_rate_per_day, rounded up to whole days; otherwise null.

- project_maturity_phase by elapsed_days: ≤7 → startup_phase; ≤30 → early_development; ≤90 → active_development; ≤180 → mature_development; ≤365 → long_term_project; else legacy_project (null maps to legacy_project).

- success_factors: concatenate, in this order, any applicable tokens separated by ", ": high_health (overall_health_score ≥ 80), strong_progress (completion_percentage ≥ 75), quality_delivery (quality_percentage ≥ 70), low_risk (risk_percentage ≤ 15), good_collaboration (unique_assignees ≥ 3), on_time (schedule_forecast is on_schedule or completed); remove any trailing comma and space; empty string if none.

- improvement_opportunities: concatenate, in this order, any applicable tokens separated by ", ": improve_health (overall_health_score < 60), accelerate_progress (completion_percentage < 50 and elapsed_days > 30), enhance_quality (quality_percentage < 60), reduce_risks (risk_percentage > 25), balance_workload (avg_tasks_per_assignee > 10), address_delays (schedule_forecast is moderate_delay or significant_delay), expand_team (unique_assignees < 2 and total_tasks > 10); remove any trailing comma and space; empty string if none.

business_logic: '1) Base rows: include tasks from staging.stg_asana__task where created_at is not null.

3) Build task stories from intermediate.int_asana__task_story where action_taken is not null and derive per task: - creation_timestamp: earliest ''created'' story, - first_assignment_timestamp: earliest ''assigned'' story, - last_assignment_timestamp: latest ''assigned'' story, - last_modification_timestamp: latest story across all actions, - completion_timestamp: earliest ''completed'' story, - Activity aggregates: total_story_events (count), unique_action_types (distinct action_taken), days_with_activity (distinct calendar dates of stories).

4) Compute lifecycle durations: - hours_to_assignment: hours from task.created_at to first_assignment_timestamp when first_assignment_timestamp exists; otherwise null, - hours_assigned_to_completion: hours from first_assignment_timestamp to task.completed_at when both exist; otherwise null, - total_lifecycle_hours: hours from task.created_at to task.completed_at if completed, else to the current time, - avg_daily_activity_rate: if lifecycle days from task.created_at to task.completed_at or current time > 0, then total_story_events divided by that day count rounded to two decimals; otherwise equals total_story_events.

• If not completed: ''stalled_unassigned'' when hours_to_assignment is null and total_lifecycle_hours>168; ''stalled_assigned'' when hours_to_assignment is not null and total_lifecycle_hours>720; ''urgent_delayed'' when urgency_score>=4 and total_lifecycle_hours>72; else ''in_progress''.
• Response speed: response_time_days<=1=30; <=3=25; <=7=20; <=14=15; non-null else=10; null=5.

6) Pattern lists (tokens evaluated in fixed order, joined by ", ", and trimmed; empty string if none): - anomaly_patterns: ''delayed_assignment'' if hours_to_assignment>336; ''prolonged_execution'' if hours_assigned_to_completion>1440; ''dormant_task'' if avg_daily_activity_rate<0.1 and not completed; ''overengineered_simple'' if complexity_score=1 and total_lifecycle_hours>336; ''urgent_ignored'' if urgency_score>=4 and response_time_days>3; ''blocked_subtask'' if parent_task_id not null and total_lifecycle_hours>720; ''severely_delayed'' if delay_days>14; ''high_churn'' if total_story_events>50.

7) Project context: join staging.stg_asana__project_task on task_id, then staging.stg_asana__project left-joined to intermediate.int_asana__project_health_indicators to get project_name, team_id, and project_health_score (defaults to 50 when the project exists without indicators).
Tasks with multiple projects yield one row per membership; tasks without a project retain a single row with null project fields.

9) Relative performance vs project: compare lifecycle_health_score to project_health_score and assign: >+20 ''above_project_average''; >+10 ''slightly_above_average''; >= -10 ''project_average''; >= -20 ''slightly_below_average''; else ''below_project_average'' (null project score falls into ''below_project_average'').

10) Data quality validation (is_valid_record): mark false when task_id or task_name is null; lifecycle_health_score outside [0,100]; any of total_lifecycle_hours, hours_to_assignment, hours_assigned_to_completion, or avg_daily_activity_rate is negative; or is_completed=true while both completion_timestamp and completed_at are null.

- Defaulting for missing current-month rows via COALESCE: - Numeric: total_tasks_assigned, tasks_completed, completion_rate_pct, quality_rate_pct, avg_completion_time, avg_health_score, total_complexity_points -> 0.
- Left join to users (cast user_id as varchar) and default missing baseline fields to 0; historical_months defaults to 0 when baseline absent.
4) Baseline deltas: - completion_rate_vs_baseline = round(current_completion_rate - baseline_completion_rate, 2) if baseline_completion_rate > 0 else NULL.
- completion_time_vs_baseline_pct = round(((current_avg_completion_time - baseline_completion_time) * 100.0 / baseline_completion_time), 2) if baseline_completion_time > 0 else NULL.
- health_score_vs_baseline = round(current_health_score - baseline_health_score, 2) if baseline_health_score > 0 else NULL.
5) Task portfolio (current snapshot): - From intermediate.int_asana__task_performance_metrics where assignee_user_id IS NOT NULL and is_valid_record = true; group by assignee_user_id.
- Averages: avg_portfolio_health = avg(health_score); avg_urgency_score = avg(urgency_score) over rows with due_date IS NOT NULL.
- Averages exclude NULL values; left join to users (cast ids as varchar); default missing portfolio aggregates to 0; no de-duplication beyond grouping key.

- improvement_recommendations: evaluate conditions in fixed order and join labels with ", " then trim trailing delimiter: 1) current_completion_rate < 70 -> "improve_completion_rate" 2) current_quality_rate < 60 -> "focus_on_quality" 3) overdue_tasks > 0 -> "address_overdue_tasks" 4) high_priority_tasks > total_assigned_tasks*0.5 -> "prioritize_effectively" 5) current_avg_completion_time > baseline_completion_time*1.5 -> "improve_efficiency" 6) avg_portfolio_health < 60 -> "improve_task_health" - If none apply -> empty string; label order is deterministic as listed; delimiter is ", ".
- is_valid_record = true iff: user_id and user_name are non-null; comprehensive_performance_score in [0,100]; current_completion_rate and current_quality_rate in [0,100]; portfolio_task_count >= 0.

business_logic: '- Build install_cohorts: - From staging.stg_google_play__stats_installs_country select rows with date_day not null and both daily_device_installs > 0 and daily_user_installs > 0.
- Map retention_period only for exact days_since_install in {0,1,7,14,30,60,90}; others => null.
- For each period in {1,7,14,30,60,90}, compute retention_rate = (capped retained / cohort_size) * 100, rounded to 2 decimals; null if the retained count is missing.
- daily_churn_rate = (uninstalls / active_devices) * 100, rounded to 4 decimals when active_devices > 0; else null.

- avg_7d_churn_rate = 7-row rolling average by date_day within (package_name, country) of (uninstalls / active_devices) * 100; rows with active_devices <= 0 contribute null and are excluded; not rounded here.
- retention_quality_score = 0.3*day_1_retention_rate + 0.4*day_7_retention_rate + 0.3*day_30_retention_rate, rounded to 2 decimals; null if any input is null.
- retention_category by day_30_retention_rate: >=40 Excellent; >=25 Good; >=15 Average; >=5 Poor; if not null and <5 Critical; if null Insufficient Data.
- churn_risk_level by the latest unrounded 7-day average churn: >10 High; >5 Medium; >2 Low; if not null and <=2 Minimal; if null Unknown Risk.
- retention_trend compares day_7_retention_rate to the 7-row lag: Improving if greater, Declining if less, else Stable (includes cases with null lag or equality).

- Derive product_stickiness by thresholds: if day_1>=70 and day_7>=30 Sticky; else if day_1>=50 and day_7>=20 Engaging; else if day_1>=30 and day_7>=10 Standard; else if day_1 not null Struggling; else Insufficient Data.
- Keep rows where install_date, package_name, country are not null and cohort_size > 0.'

business_logic: 'Data assembly: - From staging.stg_jira__sprint, keep sprints with started_at not null.
- planned_duration_days = (ended_at - started_at) in days when both exist, else null.

- story_points per issue: take the latest active field value whose field name contains “story” and “point”; use the numeric value if the field is numeric or extract the first numeric substring; if unavailable/unparsable, default to 1.
- time_spent_seconds and original_estimate_seconds default to 0 when null.
story_points_remaining: sum of story_points where issue_resolved_at is null or its date is after snapshot_date.
- daily_velocity: previous snapshot’s story_points_remaining minus current (null for the first snapshot; may be negative).
- scope_change_points and scope_change_issues: change in committed story points and issue count since the previous snapshot (null for the first snapshot).

business_logic: 'Build issue_enriched_base from marts.jira__issue_enhanced and compute: - total_lifecycle_days = days between created_at and resolved_at (or current time if unresolved) - assigned_duration_days = days between first_assigned_at and resolved_at (or current time) - Carry through count_comments, project/assignee fields, sprint flags Build issue_lifecycle_context from staging.stg_jira__issue providing default context per issue_id: - total_transitions=0; unique_statuses_visited=0; days_in_development=0; days_in_qa=0; days_in_intake=0 - regression_ratio=0.0; progress_efficiency=1.0; lifecycle_pattern=''Normal''; lifecycle_quality_score=75.0 - resolution_speed_category=''Standard Timeline''; high_complexity_risk=false Build issue_comparative_metrics via a self-join on project_id (ieb ⋈ ieb2): - Window metrics over ieb2 partitions: - project average/median/p75 lifecycle days by ieb.project_id - issue type average/median lifecycle days by ieb.issue_type - priority average lifecycle days by ieb.current_priority - assignee average lifecycle days and total issues by ieb.assignee_user_id - project average comments and issue type average comments - Note: The self-join creates multiple rows per issue_id; duplicates are preserved downstream Build issue_anomaly_detection by joining issue_enriched_base to issue_comparative_metrics on issue_id: - lifecycle_deviation_ratio = absolute difference from the project median lifecycle divided by that median (NULL if the median is 0 or NULL; non-negative otherwise) - type_deviation_ratio, assignee_deviation_ratio, comment_deviation_ratio computed similarly (not exposed) - lifecycle_outlier_status determined by thresholds: - more than 2×project p75 lifecycle → ''Statistical Outlier'' - more than 1.5×project p75 lifecycle → ''Above Normal Range'' - less than 0.5×project median lifecycle → ''Unusually Fast'' - else → ''Normal Range'' Build issue_risk_scoring by left joining lifecycle_context and anomaly_detection to issue_enriched_base: - age_risk_score: 10 if unresolved and total_lifecycle_days > 90 else 0 - process_risk_score: 15 if regression_ratio > 0.3 else 0 (NULL behaves as false → 0) - complexity_risk_score: 10 if high_complexity_risk=true else 0 (NULL → 0) - engagement_risk_score: 5 if count_comments=0 else 0 - assignment_risk_score: 8 if assignee_user_id is NULL else 0 - deviation_risk_score: 7 if lifecycle_deviation_ratio > 1 else 0 (NULL → 0) - collaboration_opportunity_score: 5 if count_comments > project_avg_comments*1.5 else 0 (NULL → 0) - efficiency_opportunity_score: 5 if total_lifecycle_days < project_median_lifecycle_days*0.7 else 0 (NULL → 0) - process_opportunity_score: 5 if progress_efficiency > 0.8 else 0 (NULL → 0) Build predictive_indicators from risk_scoring: - total_risk_score = sum of individual risk scores - total_opportunity_score = sum of opportunity scores - completion_probability: - resolved_at not null → 1.00 - else by total_lifecycle_days: ≤7→0.95; ≤14→0.85; ≤30→0.70; ≤60→0.50; ≤90→0.30; else 0.15 - predicted_completion_timeframe: - resolved_at not null → ''Already Completed'' - lifecycle_pattern=''Efficient'' and assignee present → ''Within 1 Week'' - lifecycle_pattern=''Normal'' and assignee present → ''Within 2 Weeks'' - lifecycle_pattern=''Complex'' → ''Within 1 Month'' - lifecycle_pattern=''Problematic'' → ''Beyond 1 Month'' - assignee_name null → ''Requires Assignment'' - else → ''Unknown'' - recommended_action: - age_risk_score>0 and assignment_risk_score>0 → ''Urgent: Assign and Expedite'' - process_risk_score>0 → ''Review Process Issues'' - complexity_risk_score>0 → ''Break Down or Reassign'' - engagement_risk_score>0 → ''Encourage Collaboration'' - total_opportunity_score>10 → ''Leverage Best Practices'' - unresolved and total_lifecycle_days>30 → ''Management Review Required'' - else → ''Monitor Progress'' Build intelligence_classification from predictive_indicators: - intelligence_score (0–100): start at 50, add 2×total_opportunity_score, subtract total_risk_score, add 15 if lifecycle_quality_score>80, add 10 if completion_probability>0.8, then clamp to the 0–100 range - health_status by total_risk_score: ≥25 ''Critical''; ≥15 ''High Risk''; ≥8 ''Medium Risk''; >0 ''Low Risk''; else ''Healthy'' - strategic_importance: - current_priority with case-insensitive ''critical'' or ''high'' → ''Strategic'' - issue_type with case-insensitive ''epic'' → ''Strategic'' - total_opportunity_score>10 → ''High Value'' - lifecycle_pattern=''Efficient'' → ''Best Practice'' - else → ''Standard'' - intervention_urgency: - if unresolved and total_risk_score≥25 → ''Immediate'' - if unresolved and total_risk_score≥15 → ''Within 24 Hours'' - if unresolved and total_risk_score≥8 → ''Within Week'' - else if total_opportunity_score>10 → ''Study for Replication'' - else → ''Regular Monitoring'' Final output preserves duplicates from the self-join and is ordered by intelligence_score DESC, total_risk_score DESC.'

- Three-month forecast average: average of net forecasts over the current and two prior offsets (skips NULLs; returns NULL when the frame contains only NULLs; may be based on fewer than three rows at the start).

business_logic: 'Compile intermediate checks and summarize into a final unioned report ordered by report_type and quality_grade (ascending): - source_table_stats (per source table snapshot with current time): - Transactions: total records; unique records by distinct transaction_id; counts of null transaction_id (null_primary_keys), null transaction_date (null_dates), null entity_id (null_subsidiaries), null status (null_status); earliest_date = minimum transaction_date; latest_date = maximum transaction_date.

- Transaction lines: total records; unique records by distinct transaction_line_id; counts of null transaction_line_id (null_primary_keys), null transaction_id (null_foreign_keys), null entity_id twice for both null_accounts and null_amounts; earliest_transaction = minimum transaction_id; latest_transaction = maximum transaction_id.

- Customers: total records; unique records by distinct customer_id; counts of null customer_id (null_primary_keys), null company_name (null_names), null email_address (null_emails), null date_first_order_at (null_creation_dates); unique_names = distinct company_name count; unique_emails = distinct email_address count.

- overall_quality_summary (single row): - completeness_score = average across source_table_stats of: for transactions, 100 if (null_primary_keys + null_dates + null_subsidiaries) equals 0 else 70; for customers, 100 if (null_primary_keys + null_names) equals 0 else 70; otherwise (e.g., transaction_lines) 85.
- primary_concern = "Records: {total_records}, Unique: {unique_records}, Null PKs: {null_primary_keys}".
- If any concatenated component is null, the whole string is null.
- metric columns not applicable are null; assessment_timestamp = check_timestamp; quality_assessment_id = MD5 of table_name concatenated with check_timestamp as text.
- metric columns not applicable are null; assessment_timestamp = check_timestamp; quality_assessment_id = MD5 of check_name concatenated with check_timestamp as text.

- Left join staging.stg_qualtrics__block_question on (survey_id, question_id) to attach block_id; if no match, block_id is NULL; if multiple matches, rows multiply further.

- No DISTINCT, ordering, or de-duplication is performed; duplicates produced by joins are preserved; NULLs propagate from left joins.'

business_logic: 'Overview - Build metrics from: - Customers: staging.stg_quickbooks__customer - Invoices: staging.stg_quickbooks__invoice filtered to balance is not null and customer_id is not null - Invoice lines: staging.stg_quickbooks__invoice_line joined to the filtered invoices - Payments: staging.stg_quickbooks__payment filtered to customer_id is not null - Keep only customers that have at least one qualifying invoice.

Invoice summary (grouped by customer_id, source_relation) - total_invoices: distinct invoice count - total_invoice_amount: sum of invoice total_amount, treating nulls as zero - outstanding_balance: sum of invoice balance, treating nulls as zero - first_invoice_date: earliest invoice transaction_date - last_invoice_date: latest invoice transaction_date - active_months: distinct count of months with invoices based on transaction_date - avg_invoice_amount: average of invoice total_amount, treating nulls as zero Payment summary (grouped by customer_id, source_relation) - total_payments: distinct payment count - total_payment_amount: sum of payment total_amount, treating nulls as zero - first_payment_date: earliest payment transaction_date - last_payment_date: latest payment transaction_date - avg_payment_amount: average of payment total_amount, treating nulls as zero; later defaulted to 0 if no payments exist Product diversity (grouped by customer_id, source_relation) - Join filtered invoices to invoice_lines on invoice_id - Only count lines where the item_id is present - unique_products_purchased: distinct count of item_ids - total_quantity_purchased: sum of sales item quantity, treating nulls as zero Activity and segments (left-join payment and product diversity to invoice summary) - Missing payment and product metrics default to 0 (dates may remain null) - days_since_last_invoice: difference in days between current date and last_invoice_date - days_since_last_payment: difference in days between current date and last_payment_date; null if no payments - customer_value_segment by total_invoice_amount: - > 50,000 → High Value - > 10,000 → Medium Value - else → Low Value - payment_behavior by comparing total_payment_amount to total_invoice_amount: - ≥ 95% → Excellent - ≥ 80% → Good - ≥ 50% → Fair - else → Poor - activity_status by days_since_last_invoice: - ≤ 30 → Highly Active - ≤ 90 → Active - ≤ 180 → Moderately Active - ≤ 365 → Inactive - else → Lost Final selection and derived metrics - Join customers to the activity results on (customer_id, source_relation) and keep only matches.

- payment_rate_percentage: - If total_payments = 0 → 0 - Else → (total_payment_amount / total_invoice_amount) × 100 rounded to 2 decimals; result may be null or non-finite if total_invoice_amount = 0 - customer_lifespan_days: - If both first and last invoice dates exist → inclusive days between them (last − first + 1) - Else → 0 - monthly_revenue_avg: - If active_months > 0 and total_invoice_amount > 0 → total_invoice_amount / active_months rounded to 2 decimals - Else → 0'

business_logic: '- Keep bills where total_amount is not null and greater than 0.
- Build bill_spend_base (one row per bill): - bill_date = transaction_date; due_date, total_amount, outstanding_balance = balance; paid_amount = total_amount minus balance treating null balance as 0.

- payment_status: - Fully Paid if balance is null or 0 - Unpaid if balance equals total_amount - Partially Paid if balance is between 0 and total_amount - Unknown otherwise - aging_status (relative to current_date): - No Due Date if due_date is null - Not Due if current_date is on or before due_date - 1-30 Days Past Due if due_date passed by up to 30 days - 31-60 Days Past Due if due_date passed by 31-60 days - 61-90 Days Past Due if due_date passed by 61-90 days - 90+ Days Past Due otherwise - purchase_size_category by total_amount: - Large Purchase (>= 10000), Medium Purchase (>= 1000), Small Purchase (>= 100), else Micro Purchase - payment_timeliness (relative to current_date): - If due_date is not null and balance = 0: - Early Payment if current_date is on or before due_date - On Time Payment if paid up to 5 days after due_date - Late Payment if 6-30 days after due_date - Very Late Payment if more than 30 days after due_date - Otherwise Incomplete Payment - Build purchase_category_analysis (one row per bill line with amount > 0): - Join bill lines to items by item_expense_item_id.

- Determine purchase_category by lowercasing the item name (if present) otherwise the line description and matching keywords: - Office Supplies: contains office or supplies - Technology: contains software or tech - Professional Services: contains service or consult - Travel & Transportation: contains travel or transport - Marketing & Advertising: contains market or advert - Rent & Facilities: contains rent or lease - Utilities: contains util, electric, or water - Other otherwise - Build vendor_performance_analysis (group by vendor_id and source_relation, then enrich with vendor names): - total_bills = distinct bill count; total_spend = sum of bill amounts; total_paid = sum of paid amounts; total_outstanding = sum of balances - avg_bill_amount = average bill amount - first_transaction_date = earliest bill_date; last_transaction_date = latest bill_date - fully_paid_bills = count of bills with payment_status = Fully Paid - payment_completion_rate = fully paid bills divided by all bills times 100 (not rounded) - on_time_payments = count of bills with payment_timeliness in Early Payment or On Time Payment - on_time_payment_rate = on_time_payments divided by bills with a timeliness value (i.e., excluding Incomplete Payment) times 100; null if none - spend_last_6_months = total spend where bill_date is within the last 6 months relative to current_date - spend_prev_6_months = total spend from 12 to 6 months ago relative to current_date - vendor_tier by total_spend: Strategic Vendor (>= 50000), Major Vendor (>= 10000), Regular Vendor (>= 2000), else Occasional Vendor - payment_risk_level by total_outstanding to total_spend ratio: High (> 0.3), Medium (> 0.1), else Low - Build monthly_spend_trends (group by spend_month_start, spend_year, spend_quarter, spend_month): - monthly_total_spend, monthly_paid_amount, monthly_avg_bill_amount, monthly_bill_count (distinct bills), monthly_active_vendors (distinct vendors) - month_over_month_growth_pct = ((current month total - previous month total) / previous month total) * 100, rounded to 2 decimals; null if the previous month total is not available or is 0 or less - year_over_year_growth_pct = ((current month total - same month prior year total) / prior year total) * 100, rounded to 2 decimals; null if the prior year total is not available or is 0 or less - Final output: - Start from bill_spend_base; left join vendor_performance_analysis on vendor_id and source_relation; left join monthly_spend_trends on spend_month_start; left join purchase_category_analysis on bill_id.
- vendor_spend_growth_pct = ((last 6 months spend - previous 6 months spend) / previous 6 months spend) * 100, rounded to 2 decimals; null if previous period is 0 or less.

- spend_efficiency_rating: - Excellent if Fully Paid and payment_timeliness is Early Payment or On Time Payment - Good if Fully Paid - Fair if Partially Paid and Not Due - Poor if any Past Due - Unknown otherwise - Joining purchase_category on bill_id returns multiple rows per bill when multiple qualifying lines exist; if no qualifying line, purchase_category is null and only one row is returned.'

- Build revenue_details from intermediate.int_quickbooks__revenue_analysis by month per (customer_id, source_relation): • monthly_customer_revenue = sum of total_amount • monthly_customer_invoices = distinct invoice count • monthly_avg_invoice_amount = average total_amount • monthly_collected_amount = sum of collected_amount • monthly_outstanding_balance = sum of outstanding_balance - Compute customer_revenue_trends by aggregating revenue_details per (customer_id, source_relation): • Define windows relative to current_date: - Last 3 months: months starting on or after 3 months ago - Previous 3 months: the 3 months immediately before the last 3 months - Current quarter: months on or after the start of the current quarter - Previous quarter: the 3 months immediately before the current quarter - Current year: months on or after the start of the current year - Previous year: months in the year immediately before the current year • For each window, sum monthly_customer_revenue; sums return 0 when a customer has revenue months outside the window but none inside; customers with no revenue rows have NULLs after the LEFT JOIN.
• acquisition_season by month of first_invoice_date: Winter (Dec/Jan/Feb), Spring (Mar–May), Summer (Jun–Aug), else Fall; defaults to Fall when first_invoice_date is NULL.

- Build customer_segmentation by LEFT JOINing customer_base to customer_revenue_trends and customer_behavior_patterns on (customer_id, source_relation), then compute: • recency_score by days_since_last_invoice: ≤30→5, ≤60→4, ≤90→3, ≤180→2, else 1 (NULL treated as else).
• monetary_score by total_invoice_amount: ≥50000→5, ≥20000→4, ≥5000→3, ≥1000→2, else 1 (NULL treated as else).
• payment_score by payment_rate_percentage: ≥95→5, ≥85→4, ≥70→3, ≥50→2, else 1 (NULL treated as else).
- Final output: • Growth percentages (3m, QoQ, YoY) are computed only when the respective previous period > 0; value = round(((current - previous)/previous)*100, 2); else NULL.
• rfm_segment via ordered rules on R/F/M; default ''Lost''.
• recommended_action via ordered rules on R/F/M; default ''Monitor and maintain''.

• risk_assessment priority: - High Churn Risk if days_since_last_invoice>180 and total_invoice_amount>10000 - else Medium Churn Risk if days_since_last_invoice>90 and three-month growth%< -50 (growth%=0 when revenue_prev_3_months≤0) - else Payment Risk if payment_rate_percentage<70 - else Volatility Risk if revenue_volatility>avg_monthly_revenue - else Low Risk • Filter out rows where customer_id is NULL and order by total_invoice_amount descending, then overall_customer_score descending.'

Build invoice_line_details by joining staging.stg_quickbooks__invoice_line to staging.stg_quickbooks__item on item_id; include only lines with a non-null item_id and a positive, non-null amount; select invoice_id, item attributes, quantity, unit price, and line revenue.
For invoice_profitability, left join invoice_details to product_cost_analysis by invoice_id and aggregate: - total_cogs: sum of total_item_cost; null if no qualifying lines exist.
- gross_profit: sum of line_gross_profit; null if no qualifying lines exist.
- invoice_gross_margin_pct: if invoice_total > 0, gross_profit divided by invoice_total as a percentage rounded to two decimals (null if gross_profit is missing); otherwise 0.
- total_quantity: sum of quantity (null if no qualifying lines).
- avg_product_margin: average of line_gross_margin_pct (null if no qualifying lines).

- profitability_tier: based on gross_profit / invoice_total thresholds (>0.4 Highly Profitable; >0.2 Profitable; >0.1 Marginally Profitable; >0 Break Even; otherwise Loss Making, including when the ratio is null or non-positive).
- customer_gross_margin_pct: if total_revenue > 0, total_gross_profit divided by total_revenue as a percentage rounded to two decimals (null if total_gross_profit is missing); otherwise 0.
- avg_profit_per_invoice: average of gross_profit (ignores nulls).
- margin_volatility: standard deviation of invoice_gross_margin_pct (ignores nulls; null if fewer than two non-null values).
- monthly_gross_margin_pct: if monthly_revenue > 0, monthly_gross_profit divided by monthly_revenue as a percentage rounded to two decimals (null if monthly_gross_profit is missing); otherwise 0.
Derivations: - customer_profit_growth_pct: if previous 6-month profit > 0, ((last 6 months − previous 6 months) / previous 6 months) as a percentage rounded to two decimals; otherwise null.
- relative_performance: compare invoice gross_profit to the customer’s avg_profit_per_invoice (Above Average if >1.5×, Average if >0.8×, else Below; a null comparator yields Below).
Aggregations follow standard null handling (aggregates ignore nulls; sums of only nulls yield null; explicit zeros are used in the 6‑month window sums).

- first_transaction_date/last_transaction_date: earliest/latest bill_date; days_since_last_transaction: difference in days from today to last_transaction_date (NULL if no bill_date).

- spend_current_quarter: sum of total_amount for months on/after the start of the current quarter; months outside contribute zero; NULL if all qualifying amounts are NULL; 0 if no months qualify.

- spend_prev_quarter: sum of total_amount for the prior quarter window (from quarter_start-3 months up to but before quarter_start); outside months contribute zero; NULL if all qualifying amounts are NULL; 0 if no months qualify.
- spend_current_year: sum of total_amount for months on/after the start of the current calendar year; outside months contribute zero; NULL if all qualifying amounts are NULL; 0 if no months qualify.

- spend_prev_year: sum of total_amount for the previous calendar year window (from year_start-1 year up to but before current year_start); outside months contribute zero; NULL if all qualifying amounts are NULL; 0 if no months qualify.
- on_time_payment_rate: on-time/early payment count divided by rows excluding ''Incomplete Payment'', multiplied by 100; NULL when that denominator is zero (not rounded).

- Compute four scores (each yields 25/20/15/10/5; NULL inputs fall into the lowest bucket of 5): - payment_reliability_score by payment_completion_rate thresholds: ≥95, ≥85, ≥75, ≥65.

- annual_spend_growth_pct: percentage change from prior to current year, rounded to two decimals; NULL when prior-year spend is not positive.

business_logic: '- Build employee_base_enhanced from intermediate.int_workday__worker_employee_enhanced (ebe): - employee_id is an MD5 of "<worker_id>-<source_relation>-<position_id>-<position_start_date>" using "-" as delimiter and replacing NULL components with "_dbt_utils_surrogate_key_null_".
- Organization context (oc): - Join worker_position_organization to organization_metrics on organization_id and source_relation; keep only current relationships (effective_end is NULL).
- work_conditions_score is the sum of three components (0–3): shift required → 0 else 1; union eligible → 1 else 0; default_weekly_hours ≤40 → 1 else 0; NULLs follow the else branch.
Compute: - age from date_of_birth relative to current_date with birthday adjustment; NULL when date_of_birth is NULL.
- tenure_group from days_as_worker: <365 ''< 1 year''; <730 ''1-2 years''; <1825 ''2-5 years''; <3650 ''5-10 years''; else ''10+ years'' (NULL falls to else).

- Default NULLs using these rules: - Lifecycle: retained_30_days/90_days/1_year/3_years → 0; churn_risk_category → ''Unknown''; employee_maturity_segment → ''Unknown''; departure_category → ''Active Employee''; tenure_years → 0; hire_quarter_cohort → ''Unknown''; hire_year_cohort → calendar year of hire_date; retention_stability_score → 0; hire_month → month number of hire_date; hire_season → ''Unknown''.

business_logic: 'Build organization-level performance by: - Start with intermediate.int_workday__organization_metrics (om) and derive: - avg_weekly_hours_per_employee: when current employees exist, divide total weekly hours by current employees and round to 2 decimals; else 0; if total weekly hours is missing, the result is null.

- span_of_control: when individual contributors > 0, divide individual contributors by the sum of managers, senior managers, and directors and round to 2 decimals; if that sum is 0 or missing, the result is null; if individual contributors = 0, the result is 0.

- talent_density_ratio: when current employees exist, divide unique compensation grades by current employees, multiply by 100, and round to 2 decimals; else 0; if grades are missing, the result is null.
- Diversity: count of distinct non-null ethnicity codes for employed workers; count of distinct employed military service workers.

- Compute additional org-level metrics: - regular_employee_percentage: regular employees divided by current employees multiplied by 100 and rounded to 2 decimals; null when regular employees is missing.
- avg_tenure_years: avg_tenure_days divided by 365 and rounded to 2 decimals; null when avg_tenure_days is missing.

- Performance rates (high_value_retention_rate, talent_flight_risk_rate, high_achiever_percentage, high_risk_percentage): each count divided by current employees multiplied by 100 and rounded to 2 decimals; counts default to 0 when missing.
- Satisfaction, diversity, veterans, age metrics: averages and counts default to 0 when missing; averages rounded as specified.
- Enhanced organization effectiveness score (0–100): weighted sum rounded to 2 decimals and always non-null: - Talent quality (30%): avg_career_development_score scaled by 0.3 and capped at 30.

- Weekly hours: - Average weekly hours are computed over active employees, excluding NULL values.
- Total weekly hours are the sum over active employees, excluding NULL values.
- Part-time counts include active employees with weekly hours below 40; full-time counts include active employees with weekly hours at or above 40; rows with NULL hours do not meet either predicate.
- Diversity: - Ethnic diversity counts the distinct ethnicity code values among active employees; NULL codes are ignored.
- Age and generation groups among active employees: - Average age excludes NULL values.

- retention_turnover_analysis: - Retention rates at 30 days, 90 days, 1 year, and 3 years are the mean of the corresponding retained flags among active employees, expressed as percentages and rounded to two decimals; if there are no active rows or all flags are NULL, the rate is NULL.

- Annual turnover rate is the percentage of distinct workers who are no longer employed and departed in the past 12 months divided by distinct workers hired on or before one year ago, rounded to two decimals; if the denominator is zero, the value is NULL.
- Tenure: - Average tenure for active employees converts average days as worker to years and rounds to two decimals; excludes NULL days.
- Average tenure for departed employees applies the same conversion and rounding; excludes NULL days.
- career_performance_metrics (filtered to active employees): - Average career development score is rounded to two decimals; NULL scores are excluded.
- Final computations: - Percentages divide the numerator by the stated denominator, multiply by 100, and round to two decimals; if the denominator is zero, the result is NULL.
- If any component is NULL, the overall score is NULL.

- is_current_quarter_created: true when created_date falls in the same calendar quarter and year as today; false otherwise (including NULL created_date).
- Output all selected columns; fields from non-matching joins are NULL; no additional filtering or de-duplication.'

- Build an active user lookup from staging.stg_salesforce__user where is_active = true; compute owner_name by concatenating first_name and last_name with a single space, treating missing parts as empty, and trimming extra spaces.
- Left join users to lf on lf.owner_id = user_id; if no active user matches, owner_name is NULL.

- Derive period flags relative to the current_date at runtime: - is_current_month is true when created_date falls in the current calendar month and year; otherwise false (also false if created_date is NULL).
- is_current_quarter is true when created_date falls in the current calendar quarter and year; otherwise false (also false if created_date is NULL).

description: True when created_date falls in the current calendar quarter and year at runtime; else false or NULL treated as false.
- full_name: concatenate first_name and last_name with a single space, treating NULL as empty string, then trim whitespace from both ends; if both names are NULL, return an empty string.

- user_type: case-insensitive classification based on user_role_name (first match wins): • contains "sales" or "account" → "Sales" • contains "marketing" → "Marketing" • contains "manager" or "director" or "vp" → "Management" • contains "support" or "service" → "Customer Success" • contains "admin" → "Administrator" • otherwise (including NULL role name) → "Other" - user_tenure_days: if last_login_date is present, compute the number of days between last_login_date (date only) and today; otherwise NULL.
- user_tenure_category: if last_login_date is NULL → "Unknown"; else bucket by days since last_login_date: <90 → "Recent User"; <365 → "Active User"; otherwise → "Experienced User".

- manager_id and manager_name: manager_id is manager.user_id from the self-join; manager_name is built like full_name from the manager’s names; if no manager match, manager_id is NULL and manager_name is an empty string.

- productivity_level: map performance_tier to: • "High Performer" → "High Productivity" • "Good Performer" → "Good Productivity" • "Developing" → "Developing Productivity" • "New User" → "New User" • otherwise (including NULL) → "Unknown" - system_adoption_level: based on up.total_activities and up.total_opportunities: • at least 100 activities and at least 20 opportunities → "High Adoption" • at least 50 activities and at least 10 opportunities → "Medium Adoption" • at least 10 activities and at least 5 opportunities → "Basic Adoption" • more than 0 activities OR more than 0 opportunities → "Limited Adoption" • otherwise (including NULL metrics) → "No Activity" - activities_per_win_ratio: if total_activities > 0 and won_opportunities > 0, compute total_activities divided by won_opportunities and round to 2 decimal places; otherwise NULL.
- All metrics from the performance model are passed through without transformation and remain NULL if no matching performance record exists.'

grain: One row per input line with non-null invoice_id and line_item_id; duplicates preserved
- Standardize amounts and quantity: - line_amount_nonneg: if line_amount is null then null; if negative then 0; otherwise keep line_amount.
- tax_amount_nonneg: if tax_amount is null then null; if negative then 0; otherwise keep tax_amount.
- line_net_of_tax: line_amount minus tax_amount (treat missing tax_amount as 0); if result is negative then 0; if line_amount is null then null.
- quantity: set to null when source quantity is null or negative; otherwise keep the source value.
- Per invoice_id, compute: - invoice_gross_nonneg: sum of line_amount_nonneg (nulls ignored; null if all inputs are null).
- invoice_net_nonneg: sum of line_net_of_tax (nulls ignored; null if all inputs are null).
- invoice_line_count: number of lines after the ID filters (includes lines with null amounts).
- Per-line shares (only when denominators are positive): - line_share_gross: line_amount_nonneg divided by invoice_gross_nonneg; otherwise null.
- line_share_net: line_net_of_tax divided by invoice_net_nonneg; otherwise null.
- Classify line_item_type by line_amount: positive → Revenue; negative → Expense/Refund; zero or null → Neutral.

business_logic: '- Input rows come from staging.stg_youtube__channel_basic, keeping only records where the source date_day is not NULL.
- Attempt to cast the source date_day to DATE; if casting fails, the resulting date_day is NULL and the row is kept.

- Replace NULLs with defaults: - views, likes, dislikes, shares, subscribers_gained, subscribers_lost -> 0 - estimated_minutes_watched -> watch_time_minutes = 0.0 - estimated_red_minutes_watched -> red_watch_time_minutes = 0.0 - average_view_duration_seconds -> 0.0 - average_view_duration_percentage -> unchanged (may be NULL) - Derived metrics: - like_rate, dislike_rate, share_rate are computed as metric ÷ views only when views > 0; otherwise NULL; computed in double precision with no rounding or clamping.
- avg_view_duration_seconds_weighted = average_view_duration_seconds when views > 0; otherwise NULL (no cross-row weighting).

- Window calculations are computed separately for each video_id, ordered by date_day ascending (missing dates are not imputed): - prev_day_views equals the views from the immediately preceding row in that order; NULL for the first row per video_id.
